channel.title: Tech Xplore - electronic gadgets, technology advances and research news
channel.description: Tech Xplore internet news portal provides the latest news on electronics, technology, and engineering.

item.title: AI translation sounds convincing, but it can be riddled with hidden errors
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are more widespread than ever, and one of the functions they offer is fast, real-time translation. Some people are even questioning the need to ever learn another language if near-instant translation is so widely available to all of us, often for free.

item.title: New coating approach aligns molecules upright to boost organic solar cell efficiency
item.description: Solar cells, devices that can convert sunlight into electricity, are now widely used in many countries worldwide. While most cells on the market today are primarily made of silicon, energy engineers have been exploring the potential of other materials that produce an electrical voltage when light is directed at them.

item.title: Laden with eggs, robots race up sacred Chinese mountain
item.description: Dozens of robots took on more than 3,000 steps up one of China's most famous peaks Monday, carrying eggs and watermelons in a race organizers billed as a test of real-world machine endurance, state media showed.

item.title: Winds of change: Laos looks up for renewables push
item.description: Rising from verdant ridgelines of southern Laos, 133 Chinese-built wind turbines help power Vietnam's surging growth and represent part of a regional rush to diversify energy sources.

item.title: Binance resumes withdrawals after more than $6 billion stolen in hack
item.description: Binance said that it had seen withdrawals of around $4.7 billion on Sunday, after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for.

item.title: Electrolyte redesign unlocks tin's full charge capacity for flow batteries
item.description: Tin is able to exchange four electrons as it changes between dissolved ions and solid metal, but acidic tin batteries commonly use only a two-electron reaction, leaving half that potential charge out of reach. Now, researchers in China have shown that changing the liquid around the tin could capture that extra capacity.

item.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some scraping
item.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being scraped to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

item.title: Meta settles, leaving Snap sole defendant in new social media trial
item.description: Meta reached a settlement in a landmark case over the alleged harms of social media, the plaintiffs' lawyers said Friday, leaving Snap as the only defendant in a trial set to open in Los Angeles next week.

item.title: What to know about the $6.3B hack on Binance, likely the biggest-ever crypto theft
item.description: Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit.

item.title: New electrode-making method offers cleaner route to sunlight-powered hydrogen production
item.description: A research team led by professor Jongmin Choi of the Department of Energy Science & Engineering at DGIST, in collaboration with a team led by professor Younghoon Kim of the Department of Chemistry at Kookmin University, has developed a highly efficient photoelectrode that produces hydrogen using sunlight through a water-based, low-voltage process.

item.title: Binance heist: How were cryptocurrency billions stolen?
item.description: Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, estimates that assets worth $6.3 billion were impacted by a hacking attack against the trading platform.

item.title: Laser pulses can track extreme airflow in tests for hypersonic spacecraft
item.description: Researchers from The University of Texas at Arlington's Aerodynamics Research Center have published a study in the journal Communications Engineering. Their work details a laser-based technique applied to arc-jet flows that could transform how scientists measure hypersonic airflow, such as the extreme conditions encountered by spacecraft reentering Earth's atmosphere.

item.title: UK probes Meta over 'exploitative' new terms for media
item.description: Britain's competition watchdog Friday opened an investigation into whether Meta was imposing "exploitative" new terms allowing it to use media content for its own products, including AI, without giving publishers adequate choice.

item.title: Robot moth grows a UV sensor by using an artificial circulatory system
item.description: A moth-shaped robot used an artificial circulatory system to deliver chemical building blocks through its body and grow a light sensor where UV light struck.

item.title: Solid-state cooling advances toward practical use, but challenges remain
item.description: As temperatures rise, the need for cooling is growing worldwide. Conventional cooling systems consume large amounts of electricity and use refrigerants with a high global warming potential. Caloric cooling could offer a sustainable alternative by using solid-state materials instead of conventional refrigerants. Researchers at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), together with international partners, have analyzed the state of development of such systems.

item.title: Fast Feature Field: The missing link between event cameras and robot vision
item.description: For decades, event cameras, which emulate the biological retina by continuously monitoring changes in light intensity, have promised to revolutionize how robots perceive the world by allowing them to react faster and operate more reliably than conventional cameras permit.

item.title: Armored caterpillars offer robot designers lessons in crossing slippery glass
item.description: Animals have long been one of the primary sources of inspiration for robotics researchers. This is because they rely on sophisticated biological mechanisms and locomotion strategies that could be artificially reproduced in robots to equip them with desired capabilities.

item.title: Researchers develop nonflammable and more durable electrolyte for sodium metal batteries
item.description: In recent years, sodium-metal batteries (SMBs) have gained increasing attention for next-generation energy storage technologies due to the abundance and low cost of sodium (Na) reserves, making them cost-effective alternatives to current commercial lithium-ion batteries. However, the practical applications of SMBs are still limited by critical safety and stability issues.

item.title: Mystery of 60-second fluctuations in power grids solved
item.description: TenneT Germany, the largest transmission system operator in Germany, has observed over several years that the frequency in the European power grid dips briefly every 60 seconds. While these deviations were not critical to grid security, they were clearly measurable and unusually regular. The cause of this phenomenon was initially unclear.

item.title: Thousands of deceptive ads evade Google's safeguards
item.description: Thousands of deceptive advertisements have slipped through Google's advertising safeguards, exposing internet users to fake virus warnings, misleading software promises and potentially dangerous downloads, according to new research from NYU Tandon and Radboud University in the Netherlands.

item.title: Engineering researcher seeks to prevent AI agents from going rogue
item.description: As artificial intelligence systems become increasingly capable of working on their own, keeping them focused on their designated tasks is a growing challenge.

item.title: Electric trucks: Reliable on the road and profitable as energy storage
item.description: Electric trucks could help freight carriers reduce energy costs and ease financial pressures: Their batteries can also serve as energy storage for the depot or the public grid. As the SPIRIT-E research project comes to a close, a consortium led by the Technical University of Munich (TUM) demonstrates how the vehicles can be integrated into the energy system and what conditions must be met for their economically viable operation.

item.title: How cities can make room for robotaxis
item.description: Switzerland recently launched its first driverless taxi service in Furttal, near Zurich. As robotaxi services become a reality, researchers are increasingly focusing not just on their technical feasibility, but on how large fleets of autonomous vehicles can be integrated into transportation systems while also extending mobility options to currently underserved rural regions.

item.title: Using ChatGPT before a medical appointment? How to get the best support for your health questions
item.description: Erin is in her early 40s. She works part time in a demanding job and has two kids in elementary school. She feels constantly exhausted; she's often angry and feels like she can't think like she used to. Her friend tells her it's perimenopause.

item.title: Platform simulates lowest-cost pathways for Brazil to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050
item.description: A new public, open-source digital platform developed by scientists at the State University of Campinas (UNICAMP) in Brazil and Princeton University in the United States promises to facilitate the formulation of climate policies in Brazil.

item.title: Shock, vindication, regret: Scientists react to AI roiling life's work
item.description: For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do.

item.title: Polymarket paused international trading after a security issue involving a third-party provider
item.description: Polymarket temporarily halted trading on its international platform Thursday because of a security incident that compromised a third-party provider, the company said.

item.title: What to consider if a company that made AI-related job cuts wants you back
item.description: Companies around the world are increasingly citing artificial intelligence when slashing jobs, fueling anxiety that a lot more workers may lose their livelihoods to machines.

item.title: Nvidia's web of AI bets: Smart strategy or bubble risk?
item.description: Nvidia's $3 billion investment in Meta's share sale, announced Tuesday, is the latest addition to a portfolio of stakes, loans and guarantees that has made the chip giant what some analysts describe as the central bank of the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binance
item.description: U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM said a North Korean hacking unit was likely behind the theft of more than $6 billion on the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance.
